# Frame Kit (@presentstandards/framekit-ui)

> Setup in a consuming repo: `npx framekit-agents` installs this skill for Claude Code and
> Codex and writes CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md context. Hosted mirrors of all docs:
> https://framekit.presentstandards.studio/llms.txt and /llms-full.txt.

> Precision React UI kit for creative and productivity tools — panels, inspectors,
> canvases, timelines. Light by default with a first-class dark theme, token-driven.
> Ships its own fonts (Inter Variable + Office Code Pro) and a 375-icon set.
> Every component ships with a machine-readable spec in docs/components/.

Start here when building UIs with this kit:

## AI direction

- docs/ai/direction.md: Required foundation brief (accent, style, themes, density, sidebar data), workflow, prompt intake, and release checks
- docs/ai/skill.md: Install and use the shared Frame Kit skill
- docs/ai/gpt-codex.md: Codex project setup and invocation
- docs/ai/claude.md: Claude Code project setup and invocation
- skills/frame-kit/SKILL.md: Canonical provider-neutral skill for GPT/Codex and Claude

## Docs

- docs/README.md: How this documentation is organized and how to consume it
- docs/principles.md: Design charter — density, color rules, motion, API conventions
- docs/tokens.md: Full design-token reference (colors, type, spacing, radii, elevation)
- docs/customization.md: Public customization order, scoped token overrides, and extension rules
- docs/icons.md: Icon usage + the full list of 375 icon names/components
- docs/components/: One spec per component (frontmatter + props + tokens + examples)

## Rules of thumb

- Import styles once: `import '@presentstandards/framekit-ui/styles.css'` (includes fonts + tokens + base).
- Dark theme: set `data-theme="dark"` on the root element. Light is the default.
- Style: base is the unchanged default. Use `data-style="transparent"` or
  `applyFrameKitStyle('transparent')` for translucent panels and raised tool
  chrome; `resetFrameKitStyle()` restores base. Keep the app canvas solid.
- Accent: graphite by default (restrained, non-colored). Presets via
  `data-accent="slate|sage|mauve|sand|blue|teal|violet|rose|coral|amber"`;
  any color via `applyAccent('#hex')`
  (re-run after theme changes); `resetAccent()` restores the preset. Never
  hardcode a hue — use the --fk-accent* slot.
- Style with semantic tokens (--fk-bg-_, --fk-text-_, --fk-border-_, --fk-accent_);
  never reference raw scale steps (--fk-gray-*) or hard-coded hex values.
- Design gaps: search exports, specs, and complete patterns first. If no component or
  composition fits, state the gap and build a private product-specific control from
  Frame Kit foundations, or add a reusable public component with its complete contract.
  Small design adjustments should use documented props, theme/accent/style APIs, or scoped
  semantic --fk-* tokens—never a divergent restyle of private component internals.
- Component choice: create a control map before composing a new tool. Consider
  the complete relevant catalogue and choose by value model and interaction.
  Do not default numeric parameters to repeated Sliders; consider AxisField,
  DragValue, Scrubber, RulerSlider, spatial, temporal, tonal, physical, and
  graphical controls when their model fits. Group sidebars by user task,
  dependency, frequency, and workflow order. Variety is not a quota.
- Primary UI text is 13px (--fk-fs-2), Inter Variable. Uppercase tags, micro labels,
  values, and code use Office Code Pro (--fk-font-mono).
- Icons: `import { MagnifyingGlassIcon } from '@presentstandards/framekit-ui'` (tree-shakeable), or
  `<Icon name="magnifying-glass" />` for runtime names. 15×15 grid, currentColor.
- Input family: `Input` handles labelled single-line values; use `font="mono"`
  and `align="end"` for measurements. `Textarea` is the multiline companion;
  `NumberInput` provides explicit application-owned step actions; `InputComposer`
  is a compact native submit form. Read `docs/components/input.md` before use.
- Stepper: `Stepper` is a bounded-value control with decrement/increment actions
  and an editable center value by default. Set `editable={false}` for display
  steppers; the consumer owns parsing, range limits, precision, and disabled
  action states. Read `docs/components/stepper.md` before use.
- Slider: `Slider` is the native-range option for regular continuous values.
  Use `RulerSlider` when a visible measurement scale helps, `DragValue` for
  direct value-field manipulation (with optional reset and bipolar fill), and
  `Scrubber` for compact inspector rows with rail, meter, or ruler feedback.
  The custom controls use Arrow keys, Home/End, and PageUp/PageDown; Shift
  selects `fineStep`, Alt selects `coarseStep`. Read the corresponding docs in
  `docs/components/` before use.
- Segmented switch: `SegmentedSwitch` is a compact radio group for two to four
  short, fixed tool choices such as frame rate or aspect ratio. Pass unique
  `{ value, label, disabled? }` options and name the group with `aria-label` or
  `aria-labelledby`. Read `docs/components/segmented-switch.md` before use.
- Tabs: `Tabs` switches between related workspace or panel views with
  `underline`, `contained`, or `soft` treatments. Pass stable `{ value, label,
content?, icon?, meta?, disabled? }` items; when every item has `content`, it
  renders linked `tab` and `tabpanel` pairs. Read `docs/components/tabs.md`
  before use.
- Checks and radios: `Checkbox` provides row and inline native-checkbox
  treatments, including an `indeterminate` state; `RadioGroup` provides native
  stacked and inline radio options. Read `docs/components/checks-and-radios.md`
  before use.
- Toggle rows: `Toggle` is a native checkbox with switch semantics for a
  standalone binary setting; `ToggleRow` adds full inspector and compact
  menu-style labelled rows. Read `docs/components/toggle.md` before use.
- Layer rows: `LayerRow` provides icon-led `layer` and text-led `preset`
  variants for compact selected-item lists. Pass a short `meta` value and
  optional icon-only `actions`, each with an accessible label. The selected row
  exposes `aria-current` and keeps its actions visible. Read
  `docs/components/layer-row.md` before use.
- Frame: `Frame` renders a named artboard boundary with optional dimensions,
  selection handles, and a controlled recording outline using `recording` plus
  `recordingProgress` from 0 to 1. The application owns canvas coordinates and
  interactions; compose `ContextMenu` around a focusable frame for object
  actions. Read `docs/components/frame.md` before use.
- Sidebar: `Sidebar` provides panel, docked, and floating inspector shells;
  `SidebarSection` keeps group labels, spacing, and full-width dividers
  consistent. Use `draggable` only with `variant="floating"`; movement can be
  parent- or viewport-bounded and supports controlled persistence through
  `position` and `onPositionChange`. To pop an individual tool out of an
  inspector, keep its value state application-owned and render the same
  controlled tool either in its docked `SidebarSection` or in a compact
  floating `Sidebar`—never two active copies. Read `docs/components/sidebar.md`
  before use.
- Easing graph: `EasingGraph` renders a cubic-bezier curve with an optional
  direct-manipulation mode. Pass a controlled `EasingCurve` and
  `onValueChange`; compose it with `Dropdown` for named presets and
  `NumberInput` for exact control-point values. Read
  `docs/components/easing-graph.md` before use.
- Camera path: `CameraPath` renders an ordered spatial route for camera moves
  and framing transitions. Pass controlled `CameraPathWaypoint[]` values with
  `onValueChange`; use `activeIndex` and `onActiveIndexChange` for the selected
  waypoint, and `snapToGrid` only when repeatable framing is useful. Each visible
  dot is a snap position. Compose it with `Dropdown`, `Toggle`, and `NumberInput`
  for a complete inspector.
  Read `docs/components/camera-path.md` before use.
- Focus crop: `FocusCrop` is a bounded crop and focal-point field for media,
  layout, and camera inspectors. Pass a controlled `FocusCropValue` and optional
  `FocusCropFocalPoint`; set `aspectRatio` plus `aspectLocked` for delivery
  framing, and use `showSafeArea` only when composition guidance is useful. The
  crop frame, corner handles, and focal target all support direct manipulation.
  Read `docs/components/focus-crop.md` before use.
- Modulation strip: `ModulationStrip` previews a procedural waveform using a
  `ModulationStripValue` with `waveform`, `phase`, `rate`, and `intensity`.
  Rate controls visible cycle density; the direct handle adjusts phase and
  intensity. Compose it with `SegmentedSwitch`, `NumberInput`, and `Slider`
  for waveform selection and exact inspector values. Read
  `docs/components/modulation-strip.md` before use.
- Tone curve: `ToneCurve` is a histogram-backed tonal transfer editor for
  luminance and individual RGB channels. Pass controlled `ToneCurvePoint[]`
  values with stable ids; middle points can be added, dragged, keyboard-tuned,
  and deleted while endpoints retain their input bounds. Pair it with
  `Dropdown`, `SegmentedSwitch`, and `NumberInput` for presets, channel choice,
  and exact selected values. Read `docs/components/tone-curve.md` before use.
- Axis field: `AxisField` is a neutral two-axis value editor for paired creative
  settings such as amount/scale or scatter/spread. Pass a controlled
  `AxisFieldValue` and `onValueChange`; provide meaningful `xLabel` and `yLabel`,
  and use `snapToGrid` only when repeatable values help. Compose it with
  `Dropdown`, `Toggle`, and `NumberInput` for a complete inspector. Read
  `docs/components/axis-field.md` before use.
- Direction pad: `DirectionPad` selects one discrete spatial direction plus a
  neutral center. Use the default `mode="eight-way"` for meaningful diagonals or
  `mode="cardinal"` for axis-only actions. Pair it with `Slider`, `RulerSlider`,
  or `NumberInput` for magnitude, strength, or distance. Read
  `docs/components/direction-pad.md` before use.
- Keyframe lane: `KeyframeLane` is a single-property temporal editor
  for discrete events, a playhead, and an optional working range. Pass
  controlled `KeyframeLaneKeyframe[]` values with stable ids and
  `onValueChange`; use `snap` for repeatable timing. The default `diamond`
  variant emphasizes events, `bar` makes holds visible, and `dot` supports
  dense supporting timelines. Use `density="compact"` when stacking multiple
  lanes with a shared playhead and range; set `showPlayhead={false}` when the
  parent provides one shared draggable playhead. Pair a selected transition with `EasingGraph`,
  and keep exact time values nearby with `NumberInput`. Read
  `docs/components/keyframe-lane.md` before use.
- Video timeline: `VideoTimeline` is a multi-track editorial timeline with
  moving, trimming, splitting, duplication, renaming, and per-lane mute/lock.
  Pass controlled `VideoTimelineTrack[]` with stable ids; persist
  `sourceOffset`/`sourceDuration` alongside start and duration. `previewSrc`
  renders native image/video previews, and audio sources are decoded once into
  a hi-res min/max/RMS peak store (`createAudioPeakStore`) painted as true
  per-pixel NLE-style waveforms per channel; pass `waveform` peaks only when
  they are precomputed away from the client. Read
  `docs/components/video-timeline.md` before use.
- Gradient editor: `GradientEditor` edits a live colour-and-alpha ramp with
  independent draggable `colorStops` and `alphaStops`. Its action bar can add
  interpolated colour or opacity stops, reverse the ramp, and remove the current
  selection while preserving two stops per lane. Use the active-segment `midpoint`
  only to bias a blend, and pair a selected stop with `ColorInput`, `ColorPicker`,
  or `NumberInput` for exact values. Use the 220px `GradientPicker` beside
  `ColorPicker` in auto-sized `Popover` + `Tabs` compositions; use the wider
  `GradientEditor` in inspectors. GradientPicker intentionally omits the inspector
  command bar, uses smaller square stops, and pairs equal Hex/Position fields below
  its unboxed ramp. Both retain the same stop interaction model. Read
  `docs/components/gradient-editor.md` before use.
- Histogram scope: `HistogramScope` is a read-only luminance and RGB
  distribution view for exposure-aware inspectors — spotting crushed shadows
  and clipped highlights, not adjusting them. Pair it with `Slider`,
  `DragValue`, or `ToneCurve` for the actual correction controls. Read
  `docs/components/histogram-scope.md` before use.
- Dropdowns: `Dropdown` is a custom, accessible single-select list;
  `NestedDropdown` hosts a small anchored group of normal Frame Kit controls;
  `Disclosure` reveals optional settings inline. Read `docs/components/dropdown.md`
  before use.
- Popover: `Popover` attaches a non-modal, viewport-aware dialog surface to one
  trigger for compact actions, settings, or supporting detail. Choose a
  `placement`; it flips and clamps at viewport edges. Use `open` with
  `onOpenChange` when nearby surfaces must coordinate. Read
  `docs/components/popover.md` before use.
- Context menu: `ContextMenu` attaches keyboard-complete right-click actions to
  one focusable target. It supports shortcuts, destructive actions, separators,
  and one shallow submenu. Read `docs/components/context-menu.md` before use.
- Hover cards & tooltips: `Tooltip` is for one concise supporting phrase;
  `HoverCard` is for richer optional preview detail. Both flip and clamp in the
  viewport, open on keyboard focus, and close with Escape. Do not hide required
  information or commands in either. Read `docs/components/hover-card.md`
  before use.
- Toolbar: `Toolbar` is a roving-focus group for tool buttons and rails. Use
  its unchanged default `size="compact"` for dense surfaces or `size="large"`
  to promote all enclosed buttons to roomier 34px targets. `ToolbarGroup`
  supports click and press-and-hold flyouts. Read `docs/components/toolbar.md`
  before use.
- Accent color is a signal, not decoration.
